results.summary: Silicon Strummer turns a VGA monitor into a playable guitar fretboard with an 8x6 grid of notes. The user moves a cursor with four buttons and holds a fifth button to output a square wave tone at the selected note's frequency. The design uses a counter to generate the tone and is tested by connecting a VGA monitor and audio output. It is notable for combining real-time graphics and audio on a single Tiny Tapeout tile.

This project implements a programmable array processor that can be written to and executed. It provides an array that can be written to and executed, with results read out via dedicated pins. The design is intended for educational purposes and demonstrates a simple processing architecture. It is tested by writing data to the array and reading the results.

This project implements a UART communication interface that echoes received data back. It is designed to test UART functionality and is verified using a cocotb testbench. The design uses a simple state machine to handle serial data. It is notable for its straightforward implementation of a common communication protocol.

This project provides a bridge between an RP2040 microcontroller and a Tiny Tapeout chip using SPI. It is designed for educational purposes and demonstrates how to interface a microcontroller with custom hardware. The design includes memory-mapped registers and is tested by sending commands over SPI. It is notable for enabling easy control of Tiny Tapeout projects from an RP2040.

This project generates a VGA video signal with a simple test pattern. It is designed to demonstrate VGA output on Tiny Tapeout and is tested by connecting a VGA monitor. The design uses a counter to generate the video timing and pixel data. It is notable for its simplicity and educational value.

Tiny Blackjack is a simplified Blackjack game implemented entirely in digital hardware, with game logic as a finite-state machine and a 16-bit LFSR for pseudo-random card generation. The design fits into a single TinyTapeout tile and includes features like doubling down and real-time hand total calculation. It is tested by playing the game using buttons and observing the output. It is notable for implementing a complete game in a small footprint.

This project uses a 16-bit LFSR to generate pseudo-random tones. It is designed to demonstrate the use of an LFSR for sound generation. The output is a square wave whose frequency is controlled by the LFSR state. It is tested by connecting an audio output and listening to the generated tones.

This project is a test structure for characterizing a PLL on Tiny Tapeout. It is designed to measure the PLL's output frequency and lock range. The design includes a frequency counter to measure the PLL output. It is tested by providing a reference clock and observing the PLL's behavior.

This project implements a programmable sequencer that can generate a sequence of events. It is designed for educational purposes and demonstrates a simple state machine. The sequencer can be programmed via a serial interface and outputs a pattern on the output pins. It is tested by loading a sequence and observing the output.

This project is a demo that was originally designed for an FPGA and ported to Tiny Tapeout. It implements a simple counter and LED blinker. The design is tested by observing the LED output. It is notable for demonstrating the portability of FPGA designs to ASIC.
